How Anthropic’s Draft Bill Would Regulate AI Models

To qualify, the risk must come from a biological weapon, a model evading its developer’s controls or a cyberattack, according to the draft. That language tracks California’s AI laws, including SB 53, signed into law last year, the report noted.

Under this bill, independent evaluators registered with the Commerce Department would assess frontier models, the most advanced AI systems. Labs could pay them, but not based on results. Evaluators must report imminent risks within 72 hours, according to the report.

Only a federal judge for the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia could suspend a model, on a request from the Commerce Department. Other agencies would be barred from halting development or use.
Draft Bill Could Reshape AI Oversight and State-Level Rules

The bill would also preempt some state AI laws, meaning federal rules would override them on risk disclosure, outside evaluation, and incident reporting. Democrats have resisted such proposals, the report noted.
